text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Premier Exploration Pakistan Ltd plans to double its business in Pakistan in the next two years.
- Business leaders have decided to deposit $1,000 each in their dollar accounts to help the country repay foreign loans.

- Pakistan Muslim League and Mohajir National Movement have agreed to form a coalition government in Sindh after the MQM formally withdrew its claim for chief ministership in favour of the League candidate and accepted the office of governor.
- The government has decided to freeze utility charges on electricity, gas, telephone and other bills till the announcement of the new budget in June.
- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif got the vote of confidence in the National Assembly (lower house).

- The five-year exchangeable bond issue of Pakistan Telecommunication Company Ltd has been over-subscribed four times mainly because of the participation of pension funds, unit trusts and mutual funds.
- Abbas Mirakhor, Pakistan's representative to the International Monetary Fund, has arrived to take instructions from the new elected government.
- A chain of export processing zones is being set up as joint ventures.
- Sharif has said expatriates have deposited $150 million for debt retirement.
- The state-run United Bank Ltd has identified 650 loss-making branches for closure out of 1,700.
- Pakistan's foreign exchange reserves stood at $654.8 million according to State (central) Bank figures released on Wednesday.
- Iranian Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati will visit Pakistan early next week.
